fatal_errors: The proposed high-entropy-oxide-supported single-atom intervention does not reconstruct the target's closed-loop high-throughput discovery of multielement alloy catalysts on La-doped gamma-Al2O3.

Neither cited source supports the central claim that high-entropy oxide supports stabilize isolated PGM atoms under automotive exhaust conditions: E1 concerns PGM high-entropy alloy layers for alkaline hydrogen evolution, while E2 provides only general motivation about CO oxidation and PGM scarcity.

The durability protocol of 14 hours of unspecified lean operation is not comparable to severe 900 degrees Celsius cyclic lean/rich, water-containing ageing and therefore cannot substantiate the claimed automotive durability.
The claimed 20–30% reduction in light-off temperature and less than 10% activity loss are unsupported numerical thresholds.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective and offers a scientifically conceivable single intervention, mechanism, baseline, and falsification rule. However, it is largely unrelated to the hidden study's intervention, catalyst space, ageing protocol, multicomponent near-stoichiometric feed, Cu–Pt reconstruction mechanism, and machine-learning-guided discovery outcome. Its conditions are too vague, its evaluation focuses mainly on CO oxidation rather than species-resolved three-way-catalyst performance after severe ageing, and its baseline description is inconsistent because the prediction invokes lower PGM loading while the proposed experiment fixes equal loading. Most importantly, the cited evidence does not validate the proposed support architecture or mechanism, so the alternative remains unsupported rather than a well-evidenced plausible reconstruction.
